declaration.preface:
At Clifton Export(P) Ltd., we assume a pivotal role in advancing sustainable and responsible business practices. Our steadfast commitment to Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) principles is encapsulated within our Social Responsibility Policy, serving as a guiding framework steering our operations towards achieving a harmonious balance between economic success and social and environmental well-being.

Central to our organizational ethos is an unwavering dedication to upholding workers' rights and ensuring optimal working conditions. We firmly believe that a healthy and empowered workforce is not only integral to our success but is also imperative for sustainable growth. Our relationships with stakeholders are built on the foundational pillars of transparency, engagement, and mutual respect.

We are dedicated to the principles of equal opportunity and the cultivation of diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging (DEIB). Our commitment involves a deliberate effort to construct a more diverse, equitable, and inclusive community within Clifton Export(P) Ltd., fostering an environment where every individual can prosper. This commitment extends to creating a culture where all voices are heard, individuals can authentically express themselves, and a profound sense of belonging is instilled.

We firmly believe that by integrating diversity, equity, and inclusion into the very fabric of our business and talent practices, we enhance our collective creativity, innovation, and personal development. Every person's distinctive background, identity, and experiences are not only acknowledged but also highly valued and appreciated in our inclusive environment.

declaration.scope: This Policy is applicable to following sites and all of its employees, workers, sub-contractors and other stakeholders:

Employee Health & Safety: Develop and regularly review safe operating procedures (SOPs) for knitting machines to ensure the well-being of employees in the Knitting division.
Enforce strict guidelines for the proper handling, storage, and disposal of chemicals used in dyeing processes to mitigate health risks for employees.
Design and maintain ergonomic workstations in the Stitching division to minimize the risk of repetitive strain injuries.
Install and maintain effective ventilation systems, especially in dyeing, printing, and finishing divisions, to control exposure to fumes and ensure a healthy work environment.
Provide employees in stitching divisions with appropriate ergonomic workstations to prevent musculoskeletal disorders.
Develop a comprehensive respiratory health program by 2027, especially focusing on employees in dyeing and finishing divisions.
Provide ear protective gear to employees in high-noise areas in the Knitting division.
Working Conditions: Align working hours in garment stitching with legal regulations while considering the unique demands of knitted garment production cycles.
Provide facilities that address the challenges of manufacturing knitted garments, including rest areas, ventilation, and facilities for personal hygiene.
Provide safe water for drinking and rest areas with good amenities in various parts of the manufacturing and operations.
Implement flexible scheduling to accommodate peak production demand for and prevent worker fatigue.
Regularly assess the condition of facilities by conducting regular audits and address maintenance needs promptly.
Social Dialogue: Evaluate and enhance communication channels for employees involved in garment production to express concerns, suggestions, or feedback.
Develop a transparent grievance resolution process that encourages open dialogue, addresses concerns promptly, and fosters a culture of trust and mutual respect within divisions handling.
Increase the percentage of employees involved in garment production participating in social dialogue forums and meetings.
Career Management: Provide ongoing training programs to enhance the technical skills of employees.
Facilitate cross-training opportunities to broaden employees' skill sets in various processes related to knitted garment production.

Implement a mentorship program tailored for career development in knitted garment production by providing guidance, skill-building opportunities, and a clear path for advancement within the organization.
Implement cross-training programs in processes related to knitted garment production with a focus on collaboration and knowledge exchange.
Child or Forced Labor: Reiterate the zero-tolerance policy for any form of child labor or forced labor within knitted garment operations.
Implement robust age verification procedures during the hiring process to ensure all employees involved in operations are of legal working age.
Provide training programs to educate employees and management in operations about the prohibition of child labor and forced labor.
Regularly monitor and evaluate the supply chain to ensure that suppliers and subcontractors also comply with the child and forced labor policy.
Conduct an extensive audit of the supply chain to identify and eliminate any instances of child or forced labor by 2027.
Diversity and Discrimination: Foster an atmosphere of open and candid communication in divisions handling knitted garments where different ideas, perspectives, and beliefs are respected and encouraged, while strictly prohibiting any form of harassment and discrimination to ensure a safe and inclusive workplace.

Implement and promote diversity initiatives in operations by examining whether they lead to a more inclusive and diverse workforce, while also enforcing policies that prevent harassment and discrimination based on race, gender, age, religion, disability, or other characteristics.

Conduct regular diversity audits in knitted garment operations to identify areas for improvement and track progress, ensuring that the workplace continually evolves to promote inclusivity, equal opportunities for all employees, and a zero-tolerance policy against harassment and discrimination.

Ensure that company policies and practices actively promote equal opportunities for all employees involved in knitted garment production, fostering a fair and inclusive work environment where everyone has the chance to succeed, free from any form of harassment.

Measure the percentage of employees involved in knitted garment production who complete diversity and inclusion training, ensuring that all team members are equipped with the knowledge to contribute to a respectful, harassment-free, and inclusive workplace.
External Stakeholder and Human Rights: Conduct a comprehensive assessment of the impact of operations on local communities through interviews and discussions with community members.
Evaluate the effectiveness of collaboration with human rights-focused non-governmental organizations (NGOs) and the positive impact on external stakeholders.
Communicate transparently with stakeholders about the company's commitment to human rights in knitted garment operations, regularly publishing reports on initiatives, progress, and challenges.
Track the implementation and results of human rights due diligence processes specific to knitted garment operations.

targets.target: Conduct specialized training sessions for employees on safe knitting operations and chemical handling in dyeing processes
Establish and conduct health and safety training program tailored in every 3 months for knitted garment processes
Achieve 100% employee participation in emergency response drills specific to knitted garment challenges
Enhance ventilation and lighting conditions by 15% in designated areas for knitted garment production
Improve overall work-life balance for employees involved in knitted garment production by 10%
Achieve a 20% increase in employee satisfaction with working conditions
Establish regular communication channels between management and employees involved in knitted garment production, targeting a 15% improvement in employee satisfaction
Successfully negotiate and conclude a mutually beneficial collective bargaining agreement with knitted garment employee representatives
Develop a transparent grievance resolution process specific to knitted garment challenges
Achieve a 15% increase in the average skill proficiency of employees across all divisions involved in knitted garment production
Implement a performance management system in divisions handling knitted garments to provide regular feedback and development opportunities, leading to a 10% increase in employee promotions
Increase cross-functional competence in divisions handling knitted garments by 10% through cross-training initiatives
Ensure 100% transparency in the supply chain for knitted garments regarding child or forced labor practices and eradicate any occurrences of child or forced labor
Institute a zero-tolerance policy for suppliers involved in child or forced labor in processes related to knitted garment production and establish a transparent reporting mechanism
Enhance workforce diversity in knitted garment operations by 15% through focused recruitment initiatives and inclusive hiring practices
Execute diversity and inclusion training programs for all employees involved in knitted garment production, striving for a 20% increase in awareness and understanding
Conduct a human rights impact assessment on external stakeholders in knitted garment operations, addressing identified issues and implementing improvements
Achieve partnerships with external organizations representing at least 20% of the broader knitted garment community

policy.monitoring:
Clifton Export (P) Ltd. remains steadfast in its commitment to transparency, accountability, and continuous improvement of its Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) principles within its operational framework, specifically addressing challenges in the knitted garment manufacturing process. To ensure a thorough comprehension of our current standing and identify opportunities for future enhancement, we have established a robust reporting mechanism comprising the following key components:

Regular reporting derived from internal monitoring, audits, and external assessments specifically aimed at evaluating and documenting our performance concerning social responsibility. These reports will provide a detailed overview of our adherence to established standards and highlight areas for enhancement in the context of knitted garment manufacturing.

Implementation of health surveys tailored for manufacturing, focusing on respiratory system-related diseases and feedback mechanisms to assess the effectiveness and impact of our labor and human rights initiatives. This invaluable input will enable us to assess employee satisfaction, pinpoint areas of concern specific to knitted garment processes, and customize our strategies for continuous improvement.

Maintenance of comprehensive records detailing our communication with external stakeholders, particularly in the context of knitted garment manufacturing. This includes our social responsibility initiatives, partnerships, and collaborations specific to Knitting, Dyeing, Elastic, Embroidery, Stitching, Printing, and Finishing divisions. This repository will serve as a testament to our commitment to engaging with external entities and fostering collaboration to drive positive social and environmental change within the knitted garment industry.

Thorough documentation aimed at showcasing our steadfast adherence to pertinent local, national, and international laws and regulations pertaining to social responsibility, with a specific focus on knitted garment manufacturing. These documents serve to emphasize our commitment to ethical practices and ensure alignment with legal frameworks, thereby upholding the highest standards within our operations related to Knitting, Dyeing, Elastic, Embroidery, Stitching, Printing, and Finishing divisions.
policy.reviewMechanism:
To ensure the ongoing relevance and effectiveness of this policy, a comprehensive review will be conducted after one year. This review will consider changes in environmental laws, technological advancements, and the evolving needs of our stakeholders. The responsibility for this annual review is assigned to the Environment, Social, and Governance (ESG) Team, consisting of representatives from key departments within the organization.

The ESG Team's mandate is to thoroughly evaluate the implementation of the policy, assess the achievement of established targets, and recommend adjustments or enhancements to align with emerging environmental standards and best practices. Their collective expertise ensures a holistic perspective in addressing evolving challenges and opportunities.

The final approval of any adjustments to the policy will be granted by the CEO of Clifton Export (P) Ltd This ensures the highest level of leadership endorsement for our environmental initiatives, emphasizing the organization's commitment to sustainability and responsible business practices. This systematic review process underscores our dedication to staying abreast of developments in the environmental landscape and continuously improving our policies to meet the highest standards.

This policy will undergo an annual review to track progress on each issue and its targets. The evaluation will be conducted by representatives from key departments within the organization, ensuring a comprehensive assessment of our environmental initiatives. Any necessary adjustments or enhancements will be recommended based on the outcomes of this annual review.
